docs.summary: Resampling. Every method hands back a new [`Image`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Image) and leaves its source untouched, so the caller disposes both.
docs.remarks: The filter is a box average: each destination pixel is the mean of the source pixels its own footprint covers, weighted by how much of each it covers. For the thumbnails and mip levels this exists to serve, that is the right answer and a cheap one; it has no ringing to guard against and reads every source pixel exactly once.

members.signature: public static Image Resize(Image source, int width, int height)

docs.summary: Resamples to an exact size, which stretches the picture where the aspect ratio differs.

params.source: The image to read. Left untouched.
params.width: Width to produce, at least one.
params.height: Height to produce, at least one.

members.signature: public static Image Fit(Image source, int width, int height)

docs.summary: Resamples to fit inside a box without distorting the picture, so the result is as large as it can be while both sides stay within the box.

members.name: Pad
members.signature: public static Image Pad(Image source, int width, int height, ReadOnlySpan<byte> fill = default)

docs.summary: Places the picture on a larger canvas without resampling it, leaving the rest at `fill`. A size smaller than the picture crops it instead.

params.source: The image to place. Left untouched.
params.fill: The channel values every uncovered pixel takes, or nothing for zero.

docs.summary: Resamples to fit the box and then centres the result on a canvas of exactly that size, which is the shape a square thumbnail of a picture of any proportion takes.
